title: Pin runner container (CUDA) + validate host driver; optional GPU clock locking to reduce variance
author: Rina Kobayashi
body:
## Summary
This PR hardens the benchmark-lab matrix runner to reduce run-to-run variance by (a) pinning the CUDA userspace via container image digest, (b) validating the host NVIDIA driver against a required minimum/allowlist, and (c) optionally locking GPU clocks (and resetting on exit) for benchmark-only nodes.

Motivation: during the FP8/INT8 sprint we saw high variance on H100 clusters traced to mixed driver versions + clocks drifting/boosting differently between runs (see ENG-7429). The runner previously accepted a floating container tag and did not capture enough environment metadata to make mismatches obvious.

## What changed
- Container pinning
  - `--image` now accepts `repo@sha256:<digest>` (preferred) and the runner will resolve + persist the digest in the run manifest.
  - New `--resolve-image-digest` mode for tag inputs (uses registry API) and prints the resolved digest into the run summary so runs can be reproduced exactly.
  - The per-run manifest (`artifacts/run_metadata.json`) now includes: resolved image digest, CUDA version from `nvcc --version` (if present), `nvidia-smi` output, and `libcuda.so` reported driver version.

- Driver validation (host-side)
  - New flags:
    - `--require-driver-min=<semver>` (e.g. `535.104.05`)
    - `--require-driver-allowlist=<csv>` (e.g. `535.104.05,550.54.15`)
  - Runner fails fast if the host driver does not meet requirements, with a clear error message containing the detected driver, node name, and suggested reroute instructions.
  - Adds a best-effort check for mixed-driver pools: when running a matrix across multiple nodes, the runner aggregates driver versions and warns (or fails if `--require-driver-consistent` is set).

- Optional GPU clock locking (benchmark-only)
  - New flag: `--lock-gpu-clocks=<on|off>` (default: `off`).
  - Optional parameters:
    - `--gpu-sm-clock-mhz=<int>` (locks graphics/SM clock via `nvidia-smi -lgc`)
    - `--gpu-mem-clock-mhz=<int>` (locks memory clock via `nvidia-smi -lmc` when supported)
  - Adds safety rails:
    - Requires `--i-understand-clock-locking=true` acknowledgement.
    - Skips clock locking when MIG is enabled (detected via `nvidia-smi -L`), and logs the reason.
    - Always registers a cleanup handler to reset clocks (`nvidia-smi -rgc` / `-rmc`) even if the run fails.
  - Adds `--clock-lock-scope=node` (current) with a TODO for per-GPU scoping once we standardize device assignment.

- Better default metadata capture
  - Always captures: kernel version, container runtime, node hostname, PCIe IDs, power limit, persistence mode, and whether application clocks are supported.
  - Writes a single-line “environment fingerprint” string into the run summary to make comparisons easier in triage.

## Files / areas touched
- `cmd/matrix-runner/main.go`: CLI flags, run manifest, preflight checks
- `internal/nvidia/smi.go`: parsing `nvidia-smi` output, driver + MIG detection
- `internal/runner/preflight.go`: driver checks, image digest resolution, clock-lock logic
- `internal/artifacts/metadata.go`: metadata schema (flat JSON output)
- `docs/runner-reproducibility.md`: how to run pinned + clock-locked benchmarks
- `scripts/ci/smoke_matrix_runner.sh`: updates for new flags

## Test plan
- Local (A100 dev node)
  - Verified `--resolve-image-digest` resolves and persists the digest.
  - Verified driver-min check passes/fails correctly by overriding detected version in unit tests.
  - Verified clock-lock path executes and resets clocks on SIGINT.

- Staging (H100 benchmark pool)
  - Ran 3x repeats on a single node with `--lock-gpu-clocks=on --gpu-sm-clock-mhz=1410` and observed reduced TTFT variance (see attached run summaries in artifacts).
  - Ran matrix across 4 nodes with intentionally mixed drivers; runner fails fast with `--require-driver-consistent`.

## Rollout / usage notes
- Clock locking must ONLY be used on the benchmark fleet. Do not enable on shared clusters or Dedicated pools.
- Recommend pinning images by digest for all published benchmark results.

## Follow-ups
- Add cluster-level enforcement via scheduler constraints so mixed-driver nodes are never selected for the same matrix run (Infra-owned).
- Add a small “variance sanity” job that checks environment fingerprint drift before executing a large matrix.

Links: ENG-7429 (variance investigation), ENG-7428 (full matrix), ENG-7422 (harness updates).
commits: runner: add image digest resolution and persist resolved digest in artifacts
preflight: validate host driver version + consistency across nodes
nvidia-smi: parse MIG mode, power limits, and supported clocks
runner: optional clock locking with cleanup handler and explicit acknowledgement
docs: add reproducibility and safe clock locking guidance
ci: update smoke test for new flags and manifest fields
review_conversation: Isabella Rossi: Can we make sure we always reset clocks even on failure? Also, do we handle SIGTERM from the job runner? Rina Kobayashi: Added a deferred cleanup + signal handler for SIGINT/SIGTERM; confirmed `nvidia-smi -rgc/-rmc` is called on exit and on interrupted runs. Claire Dubois: Strong +1 on digest pinning. Can we fail if the input is a floating tag unless the user explicitly opts in? Rina: I kept tag support for local iteration, but added `--resolve-image-digest` and we always write the resolved digest into metadata; we can tighten defaults after the sprint. Irene Choi: Driver validation: please include node hostname and detected driver in the error to speed reroutes. Also skip clock locking on MIG nodes. Rina: Updated error message to include hostname + GPU SKU and added MIG detection; clock locking now logs a warning and skips when MIG is enabled. Vanessa Ortiz: Any risk of this hitting non-benchmark pools? Rina: Default is `--lock-gpu-clocks=off`; enabling requires the explicit acknowledgement flag. Added docs note and a warning banner in logs when clock locking is active. Approvals: Isabella Rossi approved after signal handling change; Claire Dubois approved; Irene Choi approved with note to coordinate cluster constraints as follow-up.
release_notes: Benchmark runner: pinned container digest + stricter environment metadata capture; optional GPU clock locking (benchmark fleet only); host driver validation and consistency checks to reduce variance.
